segments.english: Seth lived one hundred and five years, and he fathered Enosh.
segments.literal: and-lived Seth five years and-hundred-of year and-he-fathered ACC-Enosh

tokens.note: singular after a hundred, as is usual with large numbers
Hifil wayyiqtol (narrative past): of the father, 'beget'

phrases.literal: 'five years and-a-hundred year'; the smaller number comes first in Hebrew, English reorders
the object marker has no English counterpart

grammar: The age is given smaller number first: חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, 'five years and a hundred year'.
וַיּוֹלֶד is Hifil wayyiqtol of ילד: the father 'causes to bear', that is, begets.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה closes the first half, the age; the second half names the son.
segments.note: The Hebrew number order is kept in the literal line; the English line uses normal English order.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos translates the verse closely (וַחֲיָא שֵׁת מְאָה וַחֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת אֱנוֹשׁ); it confirms the plain sense and does not bear on the English wording.

segments.english: After he fathered Enosh, Seth lived eight hundred and seven years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
segments.literal: and-lived Seth after fathering-him ACC-Enosh seven years and-eight hundreds year and-he-fathered sons and-daughters

tokens.note: Hifil infinitive construct with 3rd masculine singular suffix: 'his fathering', 'after he fathered'
'sons'; with בָּנוֹת the phrase means children of both sexes

phrases.literal: 'after his-fathering'; temporal clause from preposition plus infinitive construct
'seven years and-eight hundreds year'; smaller number first

grammar: אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ is a preposition with an infinitive construct and suffix: 'after his begetting'.
The revia on שֵׁת and the zaqef qaton on אֱנוֹשׁ set off the 'after fathering Enosh' clause from the years that follow.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה separates the years lived from the further sons and daughters.
segments.note: The text counts only Seth's years after Enosh's birth: seven plus eight hundred; the total (912) comes in 5:8.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos translates the verse closely (וַחֲיָא שֵׁת בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת אֱנוֹשׁ תַּמְנֵי מְאָה וּשְׁבַע שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן); it confirms the plain sense and does not bear on the English wording.

segments.english: All the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
segments.literal: and-were all-of days-of Seth two ten year and-nine hundreds year and-he-died

tokens.note: Qal wayyiqtol (narrative past), plural, with the plural subject 'days'
feminine dual of שְׁנַיִם, in the construct-like form שְׁתֵּים with עֶשְׂרֵה
wayyiqtol; closing formula of the genealogy

phrases.literal: 'two ten year and-nine hundreds year'; smaller number first

grammar: כָּל־יְמֵי־שֵׁת is a construct chain: 'all the days of Seth', that is, his whole lifespan.
The pashta on וַיִּהְיוּ and the zaqef qaton on שֵׁת divide the verse before the numbers.
וַיָּמֹת is the short wayyiqtol of מות, closing each entry of the chapter.
The ס after the verse marks a paragraph break.
segments.note: 912 is 7 + 800 + 105 (5:6-7): the total of the years in the two verses before.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos translates the verse closely (וַהֲווֹ כָּל יוֹמֵי שֵׁת תְּשַׁע מְאָה וְתַרְתֵּי עַשְׂרֵי שְׁנִין וּמִית); it confirms the plain sense and does not bear on the English wording.

segments.english: Enosh lived ninety years, and he fathered Kenan.
segments.literal: and-lived Enosh ninety year and-he-fathered ACC-Kenan

tokens.note: the pack's lexicon calls him Cainan; here the plain transliteration Kenan

grammar: תִּשְׁעִים שָׁנָה: after a decade number the noun is singular, 'ninety year'.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה divides the age from the birth of the son.
וַיּוֹלֶד, Hifil wayyiqtol of ילד, is the verb of begetting.
segments.note: The name קֵינָן is given as Kenan, a plain transliteration without diacritics.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos translates the verse closely (וַחֲיָא אֱנוֹשׁ תִּשְׁעִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת קֵינָן); it confirms the plain sense and does not bear on the English wording.

grammar: אַחֲרֵי הוֹלִידוֹ: preposition plus infinitive construct with suffix, 'after his begetting'.
The revia on אֱנוֹשׁ and the zaqef qaton on קֵינָן set the temporal clause apart from the years.
חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה is fifteen: the unit comes first, then the ten.
segments.note: Same pattern as 5:7; the years after Kenan's birth, 815, are added to ninety (5:9) in 5:11.
